title: AI model Mythos aids discovery of critical Rejetto HFS vulnerability
key_facts: CVE-2026-61500, CVSS 9.3, affects Rejetto HFS 3.x and allows authentication bypass and code execution
Found by Horizon3.ai's Zach Hanley with Anthropic's Mythos model under Project Glasswing; published through the VulnCheck CNA on 13 Jul 2026
VulnCheck's Canary Intelligence network started detecting probes for the flaw
HFS used Math.random() output to derive the session-cookie signing key and exposed values from the same stream during login
Mythos connected the weak random-number generator and the leaked values into a working chain
An earlier HFS flaw, CVE-2024-23692, is in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
quote_evidence: A Rejetto HFS vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-61500 (CVSS score of 9.3), discovered with the help of the Anthropic Mythos AI model is now being exploited in the wild, turning an interesting security research experiment into a much more practical warning for defenders.
Earlier today, VulnCheck‘s Canary Intelligence network started detecting probes for CVE-2026-61500
why_it_matters_hint: AI-assisted flaw discovery is being followed quickly by attacker probing.
notes: SC Media page blocked (HTTP 403); written from Security Affairs. Tech Times (URL dated 5 Oct 2026) says exploitation began within 24 hours of disclosure and is only the second in-the-wild case from Project Glasswing; those claims conflict with the 13 Jul 2026 publication date and were not used. Security Affairs's headline says 'exploiting' but its text describes probes.
